examples.title: Use StencilEvalContext

items.description: Evaluates safe stencil binding expressions. The grammar is deliberately tiny: literals, bare identifiers that read the element's props, the built-ins size.w, size.h and repeat.index, arithmetic and comparison operators, ?? and ternary conditionals, and the single permitted function token(key, fallback). Any other call is a parse error. The public evaluation APIs never throw — an unparseable or nonsensical expression yields StencilValue.Null — so a broken stencil pack cannot take the editor down.

members.name: Evaluate
members.description: Parses and evaluates expression; malformed input returns the raw string and never throws.

examples.title: Use StencilEvaluator

items.description: A parsed safe binding expression. Public parsing APIs never throw on malformed input: they return a literal-mode instance with IsMalformed set to true. The only permitted function call is token(key); any other call becomes a parse error and is handled by the same literal fallback. Parse once and hand the instance to StencilEvaluator.Evaluate to avoid re-parsing in hot render paths.

members.name: Parse
members.description: Parses text; on failure returns a literal fallback and never throws.

members.name: TryParse

items.description: Produces a clean, interaction-free SVG RenderFragment for a single WireframePage. This is the shared presentation layer reused by the live canvas and by headless server-side rendering (IWireframeSvgRenderer), so the visual stays in one place and previews cannot drift from the editor. It renders only presentation: the page <svg> root plus connector arrow markers (and an optional grid) in <defs>, the page background, visible connector paths and their labels, and each element as a translated inner-<svg> viewport hosting the component.

items.description: Floating context menu for the wireframe editor. Rendered at screen coordinates via position:fixed. Supports Canvas, Element and MultiSelect menu variants.

SVG-based wireframe canvas. Renders WireframeDocument elements as scalable SVG shapes and handles pan, zoom, drag-move, resize (8-handle), rubber-band multi-select, element drop from toolbox, keyboard nudge, and context menu. Communicates with wireframe-designer.js for all mouse/touch interactions. All mutations go through the cascaded WireframeCommandStack when available. Typically used as a child of TmWireframeEditor rather than directly.

items.description: Top-level wireframe editor component. Composes the canvas, toolbox, properties panel, minimap, and toolbar into a fully working editor. Creates and owns a WireframeCommandStack (undo/redo) and exposes it to all child components via CascadingValue. Supports JSON import/export, SVG export, zoom, grid, read-only mode, and collapsible panels. Tool mode (Select/Pan) can be switched via toolbar buttons or keyboard shortcuts V/H. Canvas size is editable from the toolbar.

examples.title: Basic wireframe editor with two-way binding
Read-only viewer (no toolbox/props)
examples.code:
<TmWireframeEditor Document="_document"
                   ReadOnly="true"
                   ShowToolbox="false"
                   ShowPropertiesPanel="false"
                   ShowToolbar="false" />

examples.title: Editor without grid, custom canvas size
Persist document to server on every change
examples.code:
<TmWireframeEditor @bind-Document="_document"
                   DocumentChanged="SaveAsync" />

@code {
    private WireframeDocument _document = new();

    private async Task SaveAsync(WireframeDocument doc)
    {
        var json = WireframeSerializer.Serialize(doc);
        await Http.PutAsJsonAsync("api/wireframes/my-doc", json);
    }
}

items.description: Modal dialog for exporting a wireframe. Lets the user choose a file name, output format (PNG or PDF), image scale (1x-3x, PNG only), and whether to include the background, then raises OnExport with the assembled export options.
Right-side layers panel for managing wireframe layers.

SVG minimap overlay for the wireframe canvas. Renders a scaled-down thumbnail of the full document with a viewport indicator rectangle. Clicking or dragging on the minimap pans the main canvas. Selected elements are highlighted. Typically rendered as an overlay inside TmWireframeDesignerCanvas via TmWireframeEditor.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the minimap wrapper.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description: Document whose elements are rendered in the minimap.

parameters.name: NavigateRequested
parameters.description: Raised when the user clicks/drags on the minimap. Parent should pan the canvas to the requested centre point.

parameters.name: SelectedIds
parameters.description: Currently selected element IDs – highlighted in the minimap.

parameters.name: Viewport
parameters.description: Current visible viewport region in document coordinates. Updated by the canvas on pan/zoom.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Width of the minimap in pixels.

relatedTypes.name: MinimapViewport
relatedTypes.description: Current viewport region: X, Y, Width, Height in document coordinates.

relatedTypes.name: MinimapNavigateArgs
relatedTypes.description: Navigate-to request: CentreX, CentreY in document coordinates.

examples.title: Minimap bound to canvas viewport
examples.code:
<TmWireframeMinimap Document="_document"
                    SelectedIds="_selectedIds"
                    Viewport="_viewport"
                    Width="180"
                    NavigateRequested="OnMinimapNavigate" />

@code {
    private MinimapViewport? _viewport;

    private async Task OnMinimapNavigate(MinimapNavigateArgs args)
    {
        if (_canvas is not null)
            await _canvas.ScrollTo(args.CentreX, args.CentreY);
    }
}

items.description: Properties panel for the wireframe editor. Shows editable fields for the currently selected element(s). Supports single-select (all PropDef fields grouped by category, plus Layout X/Y/W/H and Element/ZIndex sections) and multi-select (intersection of common props, Mixed indicator when values differ). All mutations are routed through the cascaded WireframeCommandStack when available. Text and number inputs use per-field debounce (350 ms); dropdowns and checkboxes apply immediately. Changing a size prop with SizePresets defined automatically resizes the element.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the panel wrapper.

parameters.name: ComponentScope
parameters.description: Optional application scope used to resolve custom wireframe components.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description: Document being edited.

parameters.name: DocumentChanged
parameters.description: Raised after every property change.

parameters.name: OnCopyStyle
parameters.description: Raised when the user requests copy style from the selected element.

parameters.name: OnPasteSize
parameters.description: Raised when the user requests paste size to the selected elements.

parameters.name: OnPasteStyle
parameters.description: Raised when the user requests paste style to the selected elements.

parameters.name: ReadOnly
parameters.description: Prevent all editing interactions.

parameters.name: SelectedConnectorIds
parameters.description: Currently selected connector ids.

parameters.name: SelectedIds
parameters.description: IDs of the currently selected elements. Empty = no selection shown.

examples.title: Properties panel bound to canvas selection
examples.code:
<TmWireframeDesignerCanvas @ref="_canvas"
                           Document="_document"
                           DocumentChanged="d => _document = d"
                           OnSelectionChanged="ids => _selectedIds = ids" />

<TmWireframePropertiesPanel Document="_document"
                             DocumentChanged="d => _document = d"
                             SelectedIds="_selectedIds" />

@code {
    private WireframeDocument _document = new();
    private string[] _selectedIds = [];
}

items.description: Draggable component palette for the wireframe editor. Displays all registered WireframeComponentDef entries grouped by category with a search filter. Items are draggable onto TmWireframeDesignerCanvas via HTML drag-and-drop (data-component-type attribute). Custom components registered via IWireframeComponentProvider appear in a separate 'Custom' tab. Typically used as a child of TmWireframeEditor rather than directly.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the toolbox wrapper.

parameters.name: ComponentScope
parameters.description: Optional application scope used to resolve custom wireframe components.

parameters.name: OnComponentActivated
parameters.description: Raised when the user activates a component via keyboard (Enter/Space). Payload is the component type string (e.g. 'TmButton').

examples.title: Toolbox inside a custom editor layout
examples.code:
<TmWireframeToolbox OnComponentActivated="OnActivated" />

@code {
    private void OnActivated(string type)
    {
        // Add element to canvas at default position
        Console.WriteLine($"Activated: {type}");
    }
}
